Ovdal Tûngr: Taking the Dwarven Home to Sea

Survey region (English ranking table): Bulwar.

At a glance: Keep a coastal hold alive through fleets and trade routes, then use steam engineering to build a home at sea.

Story: High | Mission tree: Long (38 definitions, including conditionally unlocked continuations) | Mission-tree update: A new tree was discussed in a 2024 development diary and is now implemented locally | Distinctiveness: Very high | Tedium: High | Early pressure: Medium-high | Expansion: Strong at sea, moderate on land.

Identity and History

In 1444, Ovdal Tûngr (F23) is a Copper Dwarf clan republic that follows Ancestor Worship, with its capital in the coastal hold of the same name. It lies in Bahar in western Bulwar, facing the Divenhal Sea. Crathánor is a historic friend; the surface-dwelling goblin neighbor and another republic are rivals. [Local history script]

The hold's defining feature is its openness to the sea. The offline English Wiki recounts that sabotage during an ancient war flooded its mines, and that records of its foundation were lost. Later, the God-King called the Benevolent invited Dwarves to resettle it; migrants from other holds restored its drydocks and made it a center of maritime trade. Jaher later seized its outlying lands in 1010 and blockaded the hold; the Wiki says the blockade ended only in 1162. This long history helps explain the Copper Dwarves' determination to secure independent trade routes. The dates of the ancient resettlement differ between sources, however, so they should not be forced into a single undisputed chronology. [Wiki]

National Story and Campaign Arc

The mission tree's future begins with reorganizing the neighbors and reclaiming influence in Bahar. Trade cannot be restored by quietly developing in a safe corner: you must deal with surface rivals, fleet strength, diplomacy, and control of trade routes before the hold can become an economic center capable of supporting long-distance voyages. [Local script]

The political story follows the growing influence of the Uthojdihr. The old council's debates among multiple clans continue, but the Uthojdihr gradually take control of its agenda through commerce and effective action; the narrative allows you to accept reform immediately or postpone it. The Strongbellow Society then shifts the country's ambitions from restoring the old shipyards to steam, ironclads, and maritime engineering. The final Sea Hold is a floating fortress and a new Dwarven home: it is a future reached by completing missions, not a structure that already exists in 1444. [Local flavor text / local script]

Core Mechanics

Trade routes sustain the hold. Fleets, ports, and trade rights have to work together. Overseas routes extend through Sarhal and Haless, with the aim of turning a transoceanic commercial network into sustained income. Expansion is often about routes and ports, not simply painting inland territory; the navy therefore functions as economic infrastructure. [Local script]

Cooperation with Crathánor. Missions allow cooperation with the republic through an alliance and good relations. Crathánor's event may accept subject status or remain an ally; Crathánor makes that decision. Cross-cultural relations improve the tolerance and presence of the relevant populations, but in multiplayer the choice of overlord and the transfer of trade rights can still affect progress. [Local script]

Drainage and undersea development. The flooded mines turn Dwarven development into a problem of exploration, pumping, and dredging. Strongbellow's technology unlocks in stages, linking advisors, Innovativeness, shipyards, and production preparation. Unlocking a technology does not mean the next engineering project is immediately complete. [Local script]

From steam to the Sea Hold. The steamship stage already demands substantial cash and industrial preparation. In the current scripts, the final Sea Hold requires an Innovativeness threshold and costs 250,000–500,000 ducats, as well as 25 production in a specified province. Docking, maintenance, and upgrades after construction are handled through decisions and events. This is not an ordinary ship reward, and menu options should not be read as mutually exclusive ideologies. [Local script]

Staged Play

Early on, secure the area around the hold, stabilize the treasury, and maintain relations with Crathánor. Do not max out fleet, army, and construction budgets all at once. The Bahar missions carry concrete garrison and development costs, so do not look only at their rewards. Arrange important trade rights while diplomatic relations are still good.

In the midgame, shift attention to ports, the navy, and overseas routes, while continuing to invest in production and the hold. Strongbellow Society's advisor requirements, the engineering Innovativeness thresholds, and staged unlocks can all force waiting. A stable income and savings for key milestones fit this campaign better than trying to fight a major war while scrambling to cover engineering costs.

In the late game, accumulating capital becomes a challenge in its own right. The Sea Hold needs hundreds of thousands of ducats; short-term military strength cannot replace an industrial and trade network. This suits players who enjoy watching a country's production model change over time. If you want continuous wars and rapid mission completion, the engineering phase can be a grind. These are script-based gameplay observations, not results from an in-game difficulty test.

Mission Future and Endgame

The 38 checked Ovdal Tûngr mission definitions form a multistage campaign under the same Tag. The Sea Hold remains part of Ovdal Tûngr; it is not a separate formable country, and no successor Tag is inferred from the sea-going home. The 2024 official development diary discussed cooperation, the revival of trade, and the Sea Hold direction; corresponding features can now be found in the local missions, events, and decisions. The scripts remain the authority for their specific operation. [Official development diary / local script]

The revival also has concrete costs. The mission “Mountains Devour” changes province 527 to the country's culture and religion, removes all Goblin minorities there, and adds 25 devastation. A Bahar governance event also removes its Goblin minorities if Goblin culture has not been accepted. Cooperation in human trade therefore does not amount to universal equality. Conversely, the “Human Oarsmen” text describes hiring; neither the oars nor the population's identity is evidence of slavery. [Local script / local flavor text]

Personality and Recommendation

Production v2.1 profile: Expansion 58 / Autocracy 58 / Magic–Artifice 18 / Theme Intensity 88 / Pluralism 52. Values: Neutral 52, mixed trajectory, medium confidence. Dignity 45, Public Good 80, Personhood 45, and Restraint 35 produce a weighted 52.25, which is then rounded. Construction and cross-cultural cooperation contribute to public good; forced Goblin removal weighs against the assessment. Trade, republicanism, and expansion do not determine moral alignment by themselves.

In the early clan council phase, Autocracy is about 35 and Magic–Artifice theme intensity 25; after the Sea Gate Clan rises and engineering advances, these become 58 and 88 respectively. These are successive phases, not a permanent player choice between two mutually exclusive routes.

The v2.2 route study separately records a full baseline: Ambition 72, Power Concentration 58, Magic–Artifice 18, Pluralism Integration 52, and Restoration–Change 88. Representative checks found no substantiated major F23 personality choice, so there are 0 choice profiles. Immediate reform versus delay, Sea Hold operations, and a relationship decided by Crathánor do not create invented branches. The new route score is not part of the v2.1 matching Demo.

Recommended for players who enjoy tall development, naval trade, technological progress, and cooperative diplomacy. Avoid if you dislike long savings periods and trade-right conditions, or cannot accept the forced expulsion of Goblins in the revival story. Commercial prosperity does not erase those harms.

Community Experience

An August 2024 test-branch account described Ovdal Tûngr as a tall power supported by a small core of provinces, emphasizing its navy and trade; it also reported a possible issue with Sea Hold operations at the time. That old test feedback is not a confirmed current bug. A March 2025 multiplayer account emphasized Ovdal Tûngr providing money and running naval trade while Crathánor played the cooperative role; a reversed subject relationship could make trade-right missions difficult. The latter post did not specify an exact version, so this is experience from that group's situation only. [Community views]

Evidence Boundaries

Verified 13 October 2026 against the base Mod and translation, both supporting v1.37.5.0. The mission file's local modification time is 7 September 2026, not its original release date. Identity and mechanics follow current local sources; historical context is supplemented by fixed-revision offline Wiki material. The ancient resettlement date, the sequence linking later alliances and blockades, all Sea Hold upgrades, and DLC combinations remain unresolved. Community historical-map projections are not treated as inevitable mission outcomes. Full sources and version boundaries are in the evidence record; structured data is in the source country record.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Ovdal Tûngr (F23) — Copper Ideas

Set ID: F23_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = F23 #Ovdal Tungr
    }

Copper Traditions

No description is defined; the current name and script effects are retained without inventing flavour text.

Effects: Naval Morale: +15% (naval_morale; raw value 0.15); Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

1. Refounded by the God-King

For millennia, Ovdal Tûngr lay hidden among the mountains, its lower levels flooded, its forges long gone cold. It was not rediscovered until 2181BA, during a survey ordered by Irsakar the Benevolent, God-King of Barzišah. Upon its discovery, Irsakar gifted the hold to the dwarves of his kingdom to resettle in exchange for their service. While most of the hold was inaccessible, the dwarves quickly went to work repairing the dry docks. Soon dwarven sailors would be found in every port across the Divenhal Sea.

  • Diplomatic reputation: raw value 1 (unit unverified) (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

2. Republic of the Many Clans

With the reclamation of the hold, Irsakar declared that the dwarves would decide how to govern themselves. A council was convened of all the major clans in exile, including three remnants of the Serpentreach’s Noh-Kazaz, namely the Zonogherûd and Azgheledbul clans of Orlghelovar and the Aznezhyg clan of Lodhum. For decades, the council would convene and arguments would rage with each clan claiming legitimacy to rule the rest. In the interim, a single clan was selected with term limits of 20 years to administer the growing migration of petty dwarves from the Segbandal of the Middle Dwarovar. By 2064BA, with still no clan willing to give any other authority over the whole, it was decided that there would be no permanent ruling clan. Instead, elective governance would become law with its clan selected by the council. This was the origin of Tûngr’s Reachdwarf electorate clans ruling over a Segbandalic majority.

  • Random candidate bonus: +1 (candidate_random_bonus; raw value 1).

3. Ancient Trade Routes

Most of the dwarves in Ovdal Tûngr are your typical stock, completely unaccustomed to seafaring. That is not true for the Uthojdihr, a clan that was founded after the reclamation. Referred to derogatively as the logr-drika (water-drinkers) by other dwarves, this clan is as much at home on the water as they are underground. While not all dwarven sailors belong to this clan, for much of history they were the most likely dwarves to be found trading hold supplies with Ruby Dwarves in Oldport, competing with the copper merchants of Busirat, haggling for grain along the Coast of Tears, or buying silks in Brasan. Throughout the ancient Divenhal, there was an Uthojdihr family in every port.

  • Naval tradition: +1 (navy_tradition; raw value 1).

4. The Debtors of Bulwar

At the crossroads of Greater Castanor, Bulwar, and the Serpentreach holds, Ovdal Tûngr greatly benefited from the exchange of ideas from the rise and fall of the civilizations around them. This was most true when it came to trade policies. This administrative advantage combined with their long lives, led to the copper clans holding debts over most of the great houses across bulwar. Whenever the political tide turned against Ovdal Tûngr, they could leverage these debts to ensure their advantage. This changed, however, with the arrival of Jaher and his elven legions. To ensure the loyalty of his conquests, Jaher banished all dwarves from his realm and forgave all debts they owned. In response, Ovdal Tûngr sided itself with the resurgent Castanor led by the Sorcerer-King. When Jaher took arms against Castanor, he ordered a blockade of Ovdal Tûngr. "The Copper Enclosure" as it was called would last for over a century until the onset of the First Cinder War.

  • Trade steering: +25% (trade_steering; raw value 0.25).

5. Master Shipwrights

While copper makes for fantastic hull coating in the warm waters of the Divenhal, its heavy price prohibited its use in mass throughout the ancient world. This was not true for Ovdal Tûngr, however, sitting on their vast reserves of the metal mined from their mountain. Copper Bottoms as they are known among the humans were pivotal in the dwarven primacy along the Divenhal trade routes. These ships required less hull maintenance and lasted longer than their muscle encrusted competitors. And if the copper dwarves ever found themselves short on a trade investment, the sale of a few ships was enough to settle any debt.

  • Ship Cost: -10% (global_ship_cost; raw value -0.1).

6. Explorers of the Depths

The depths of Ovdal Tûngr were flooded long ago by unknown means. With Hul-Jorkad and its pumping equipment as one of the first victims of the Last Days, the dwarves of the reclamation lacked the knowhow to undertake the massive pumping effort required to reclaim the lower levels of the hold. In 1491, however, a visiting dwarven inventor by the name of Grun Strongbellow would propose a new hydraulic system that could drain even the deepest of mines. Soon the dwarves were not only delving the depths of their lost mines, but were also sending exploratory expeditions off the coast of Bulwar in copper diving helms.

  • Naval leader manoeuvre: +1 (leader_naval_manuever; raw value 1).

  • Marine force limit: +20% (allowed_marine_fraction; raw value 0.2).

7. Steam Power

The greatest gift Strongbellow left Ovdal Tûngr with was the design of a primitive steam engine to power his pumps. While the technology wouldn't exist for several more decades, once the steam engine was running, it wasn't long before dwarves figured out all sorts of steam powered oddities and trinkets. Only a century later would their full potential be discovered as a means to move the paddles of large ships. These "steamers" as they were called revolutionized water trade as ships could now more easily move upstream along the Suran to the ever expanding Jadd Empire and along the Alen to the burgeoning realms of Escann.

  • Innovativeness gain: raw value 0.5 (unit unverified) (innovativeness_gain; raw value 0.5).

  • Development cost: -5% (development_cost; raw value -0.05).
